Study focuses on cancer incidence/projections, qualitative experiences, literature review, molecular biology, or tool development rather than diagnostic test accuracy for ovarian cancer in symptomatic women with pelvic mass.

This is a prospective cross-sectional diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating four risk of malignancy indices (multivariable models) for detecting malignant ovarian tumors in women with pelvic masses, with surgical exploration as reference standard. It evaluates test combinations (RMI algorithms) for ovarian cancer diagnosis, meeting inclusion criteria.

This study evaluates the predictive value of Risk of Malignancy Index (multivariable model), CA-125, and inflammatory markers in discriminating ovarian cancers in postmenopausal women with adnexal masses who underwent surgery (histological confirmation). It assesses test combinations and single tests in a defined population, meeting criteria.

This study evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA (a multivariable model combining HE4 and CA125) for differentiating benign ovarian disease from epithelial ovarian cancer, stratified by menopausal status. It uses ROC analysis with histopathological confirmation, assessing test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This is a case-control study identifying symptoms associated with ovarian cancer in primary care. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests (ultrasound, biomarkers) or multivariable models for ovarian cancer diagnosis. The focus is on symptom prediction, not test accuracy of menopausal status, ultrasound, or biomarker combinations.

This prospective study validates the Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm (ROMA), a multivariable model combining HE4 and CA125, in women with pelvic masses scheduled for surgery. It evaluates test performance against histopathological reference standard, assessing a biomarker combination for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of diagnostic test accuracy studies. The selection criteria require primary diagnostic test accuracy studies, not reviews or meta-analyses of existing studies.

This study compares CA125, HE4, ROMA (multivariable model), and RMI for classifying ovarian masses in women diagnosed via imaging. It evaluates sensitivity and specificity using ROC curves, assessing test combinations and single models for ovarian cancer diagnosis, meeting criteria.

This is a clinical practice commentary on genetic risk assessment for hereditary cancer syndromes. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests (ultrasound, biomarkers) or multivariable models for ovarian cancer diagnosis in symptomatic women with pelvic masses.

This cross-sectional study evaluates serum CA-125, HE4, and ROMA (a multivariable model) at standard and optimal cut-offs for preoperative prediction of epithelial ovarian cancer in women with ovarian masses, with histopathological confirmation. It assesses test combinations for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This study evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA2 index for detecting ovarian cancer in postmenopausal women with histologically verified ovarian cancer and benign tumors. It assesses a biomarker combination (ROMA) for ovarian cancer diagnosis in a defined menopausal group.

This study evaluates conventional 2D ultrasound, CA125, RMI, IOTA simple rules, expert opinion, IOTA LR2, and 3D vascular indices for predicting malignant or benign ovarian tumors in postmenopausal women, with histopathological reference standard. It evaluates multiple tests and models for ovarian cancer diagnosis.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing HE4 and CA-125 biomarkers for ovarian cancer diagnosis. The selection criteria require primary diagnostic test accuracy studies, not reviews.

This diagnostic study evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA (a combination of both) for detecting ovarian malignancy in women with pelvic masses. It measures sensitivity, specificity, and AUC with histopathological reference, assessing a biomarker combination for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This prospective study evaluates HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI for diagnosing epithelial ovarian cancer in women with complex pelvic masses. It assesses test combinations and single biomarkers with histopathological reference, meeting criteria for diagnostic test accuracy studies.

This is a methodological paper introducing PROBAST, a tool for assessing risk of bias in prediction model studies. It is not a diagnostic test accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This study evaluates the performance of ROMA (a multivariable model combining HE4 and CA125) for estimating risk of epithelial ovarian cancer in women with pelvic masses. It uses ROC analysis with histopathological confirmation, assessing a test combination for ovarian cancer diagnosis.

This study defines a methodology to categorize routes to cancer diagnosis using administrative data in England. It does not evaluate diagnostic tests (ultrasound, biomarkers) or multivariable models for ovarian cancer diagnosis in women with pelvic masses.
Methodological paper on bivariate meta-analysis, not a diagnostic accuracy study evaluating tests for ovarian cancer in women with pelvic mass.
